messages:
incident-bot: SEV 2 alert: policy-evaluator service (smart-routing) reporting repeated runtime panics -> fallback/region-loop. Triggering paging to oncall. link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/1845123456 :rotating_light:

miguel_oncall: reading it now, paging ack. I see a spike in 'policy_eval_error' and a correlated increase in cross-region fallbacks. Investigating logs and routing metrics.

maria_eng-routing: adding logs here — policy id = pr-serve-09, last deploy 2026-02-12 by @sam_eng-runtime commit c3f4b2a. Recent traffic shows many eval failures: 1xx/s -> 20xx/s over the last minute. sample stack: ```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 47 [running]:
redwood/policyengine.(*Evaluator).Eval(0xc0001a2000, 0xc0002d4b80, 0x0)
	/opt/redwood/policyengine/eval.go:312 +0x1b4
main.handleRequest(0xc00032c3c0)
	/opt/redwood/smart-routing/handler.go:178 +0x2f0
```

maria_eng-routing: suspicious expression in policy ruleset (from repo): ```
when request.meta.region == "eu-west" && request.loadFactor > 0.8 {
  prefer model_variant("gptx-high") / request.weight
}
```
This can panic when request.meta is null or request.weight is zero (division). need a guard.

sam_eng-runtime: agree — quick mitigation is to disable the offending policy while we patch. runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/policy-eval-panic No-DRS steps: `redwoodctl policy disable pr-serve-09 --by miguel_oncall --reason "panic & fallback loop"`

miguel_oncall: running command now: `redwoodctl policy disable pr-serve-09 --by miguel_oncall --reason "panic & fallback loop"` -> response: OK disabled (etag: a7f9c). Applying immediate routing default to regional fallback policy v-stable-1 as additional guard.

incident-bot: ACTION: policy pr-serve-09 disabled by miguel_oncall at 2026-03-15T18:04:20Z. Auto-checks running.

amy_cs: what customers are impacted? any paying tenants seeing errors/timeouts? need to prepare outbound comms if >5% of production traffic.

miguel_oncall: preliminary metrics from console: ~18% of requests hitting smart-routing saw eval errors and then regional reroutes. Top impacted: client-alpha (10%), client-beta (4%), internal testbeds (4%). Error rate reduced to ~8% after policy disable but latency still elevated for some requests.

eng-platform: as a short-term safety net, push a route-default override to prefer local model variants (redwood-small) for the next 30m to reduce cross-region fallbacks: `redwoodctl routing override set --scope global --fallback-model redwood-small --ttl 30m --by eng-platform`

maria_eng-routing: did that override; confirming traffic shifted. metrics show fallbacks dropped ~75%. error rate now ~3%. looks like disabling policy + override is working as mitigation.

sam_eng-runtime: we should also hotfix the policy evaluator to guard against nil meta and divide by zero. Proposed code change (policy DSL): ```
when request.meta?.region == "eu-west" && request.loadFactor > 0.8 && request.weight > 0 {
  prefer model_variant("gptx-high")
}
```
This removes the division and adds a safe-null operator. I'll open a PR and cut a cherry-pick to release-2026-03-15.

miguel_oncall: creating incident ticket and recording timeline. Will handoff to next oncall in 30m. Leaving steps triaged: 1) policy disabled 2) routing override active 3) PR opened for sanitizer + unit tests 4) postmortem scheduled.

eng-platform: PR link posted: https://git.redwood.ai/policy/pr/4523 (hotfix + tests). CI green for evaluate unit tests, staging load looks good. Recommend rolling hotfix to prod with canary 5% -> 30% -> 100% after 10m checks.

amy_cs: I'll draft a short customer incident update for status.redwood.ai: "We're investigating a smart-routing policy evaluation error causing increased latency and fallbacks for some requests. We've disabled the offending policy and applied a temporary routing override. A fix is being rolled out. We'll update within 60 minutes." Tagging account managers for client-alpha and client-beta.

miguel_oncall: initiating canary deploy of hotfix now (sam_eng-runtime). `deployctl canary --service policy-evaluator --image policy-eval:hotfix-4523 --percent 5` -> canary started.

incident-bot: Canary deploy at 2026-03-15T18:18:30Z. Automated checks: 0/5 anomalous traces.

maria_eng-routing: after canary, no new panics observed on the canary cohort for 12 minutes. Proceeding to ramp.

sam_eng-runtime: ramping to 30% -> 100%. All checks green. rolling to 100% now.

incident-bot: policy-evaluator hotfix rolled to 100% at 2026-03-15T18:41:02Z. Post-rollout monitor: error rate back to baseline ~0.2%, fallbacks normal.

amy_cs: sending customer update now, marking impacted customers notified.

miguel_oncall: handoff note -> I'm handing off to alex_oncall for the 20:00-04:00 shift. Key things to monitor: policy-eval error metric, routing fallback rate, top client error counts. Runbook link + mitigation commands posted above.

alex_oncall: acked. thanks @miguel_oncall — picking up. I'll watch the dashboard for 2h and keep CS updated if anything regresses.

eng-platform: please add a regression test to the policy-eval suite for null meta + zero weight cases, and add lint rule to disallow division in policy DSL without guard.

sam_eng-runtime: will follow up with postmortem doc and action items: (1) add static analysis + runtime guards (2) stricter canary thresholds for policy rollouts (3) customer communication improvements for mid-severity incidents.

amy_cs: thanks everyone. posting to status page and sending emails to impacted accounts.

miguel_oncall: closing immediate incident channel and moving to postmortem thread. Will set SLO impact and P0/P1 customer list in the ticket. Good job all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to 'monitoring' at 2026-03-15T19:05:00Z. Postmortem owner: sam_eng-runtime.
